statuses.name: Strategic
statuses.description: Default choice for new work — actively invested in and encouraged.

statuses.name: Current
statuses.description: Approved standard. Fine to use for new work.

statuses.name: Contain
statuses.description: Allowed for existing use only — do not start new use without an exception.

statuses.name: Sunset
statuses.description: Being retired. Do not start new use; migrate existing use to the listed replacement by the target date.

statuses.name: Retired
statuses.description: Prohibited. No longer allowed anywhere, including existing use.

statuses.name: Emerging
statuses.description: Trial/pilot only. Requires architecture review approval before use beyond a sanctioned pilot.

entries.name: Azure App Service
entries.notes: Default PaaS compute for web/API workloads.

entries.name: Azure Kubernetes Service
entries.notes: Default platform for containerized microservices at scale.

entries.name: Azure Container Apps
entries.notes: Approved for pilot use on new event-driven/microservice workloads; not yet the default over AKS for production-critical services.

entries.name: Azure Functions
entries.notes: Approved for event-driven and lightweight serverless workloads.

entries.name: Azure Virtual Machines
entries.notes: Allowed only for lift-and-shift of existing workloads with a documented PaaS migration plan; not for new greenfield builds.

entries.name: Azure Service Fabric
entries.notes: Superseded by AKS as the standard container orchestration platform.

entries.name: On-premises VMware
entries.replacement: Azure Virtual Machines (contained) or Azure App Service
entries.notes: Data center exit complete; no new on-prem VM workloads permitted.

entries.name: Azure SQL Database
entries.notes: Default relational database for new OLTP workloads.

entries.name: Azure Database for PostgreSQL
entries.notes: Approved for workloads requiring native PostgreSQL compatibility.

entries.name: SQL Server on a VM
aliases: sql server on a virtual machine
entries.notes: Migrate to managed Azure SQL to shed patching/backup overhead and licensing cost.

entries.name: Oracle Database
entries.notes: Existing licensed workloads only; new projects require an exception given licensing cost.

entries.name: MongoDB Atlas
entries.notes: Not on the approved catalog — data residency and billing must stay within the Azure tenant.

entries.name: IBM DB2
entries.notes: Mainframe database platform being decommissioned org-wide.

entries.name: Azure Cosmos DB
entries.notes: Default globally-distributed NoSQL/document database.

entries.name: Self-hosted MongoDB
entries.notes: Operational and patching burden not accepted for a database tier we already have a managed equivalent for.

entries.name: Azure Blob Storage
entries.notes: Default object storage.

entries.name: Azure Data Lake Storage
entries.notes: Approved for analytics/data-lake workloads requiring hierarchical namespace.

entries.name: Amazon S3
entries.notes: Single-cloud (Azure) policy for object storage; no new S3 usage.

entries.name: On-premises file share
entries.replacement: Azure Blob Storage or Azure Files
entries.notes: On-prem storage being decommissioned as part of data center exit.

entries.name: Azure Service Bus
entries.notes: Default for enterprise messaging (queues/topics).

entries.name: Azure Event Hubs
entries.notes: Approved for high-throughput event streaming.

entries.name: Azure Event Grid
entries.notes: Approved for event routing/pub-sub between services.

entries.name: Self-managed Apache Kafka
entries.notes: Existing clusters only; new projects should use Event Hubs' Kafka-compatible endpoint instead of operating Kafka.

entries.name: IBM MQ
entries.notes: Legacy enterprise messaging platform being retired.

entries.name: Self-hosted RabbitMQ
entries.notes: Operational burden of self-managed brokers not accepted where a managed equivalent exists.

entries.name: Microsoft Entra ID
entries.notes: Enterprise identity provider of record.

entries.name: Azure AD B2C
entries.notes: Approved for customer-facing identity (CIAM).

entries.name: Okta
entries.notes: Superseded by Entra ID as the single enterprise identity provider.

entries.name: Auth0
entries.notes: Not approved for new customer-identity workloads.

entries.name: Azure Key Vault
entries.notes: Mandatory for all secrets, keys, and certificates.

entries.name: Self-hosted HashiCorp Vault
entries.notes: Existing integrations only; new projects must use Key Vault.

entries.name: GitHub Actions
entries.notes: Default CI/CD platform.

entries.name: Azure DevOps Pipelines
entries.notes: Approved alternative CI/CD platform, primarily for teams already standardized on Azure Boards.

entries.name: Self-hosted Jenkins
entries.notes: Being retired in favor of managed CI/CD; stop onboarding new pipelines to Jenkins.

entries.name: CircleCI
entries.notes: Not on the approved CI/CD catalog.

entries.name: Azure Monitor
entries.notes: Default observability platform (metrics, logs, alerting, tracing).

entries.name: Datadog
entries.notes: Existing contracted usage only; new workloads should standardize on Azure Monitor.

entries.name: Splunk
entries.notes: On-prem Splunk deployment being retired as part of observability consolidation.

entries.name: Azure Front Door
entries.notes: Default global entry point (CDN + WAF + load balancing).

entries.name: Azure API Management
entries.notes: Approved API gateway platform.

entries.name: Cloudflare
entries.notes: Not approved for production edge/CDN traffic.

entries.name: Azure OpenAI Service
entries.notes: Approved for sanctioned pilots only; broader production use requires architecture review sign-off on data handling and cost controls.

entries.name: Azure Databricks
entries.notes: Approved for large-scale data engineering and ML workloads.

entries.name: Azure Synapse Analytics
entries.notes: Approved for enterprise data warehousing.
